# DataQ backend image — serves both the FastAPI API and the Celery worker.

# ── Builder: install deps into an isolated venv ──────────────────────────────
FROM python:3.13-slim AS builder

ENV PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1 \
    PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1

# build-essential covers any sdist-only transitive dep; it lives ONLY in this
# stage and never reaches the final image.
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends build-essential \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN python -m venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH

# Copy just the requirements chain first so this layer caches on pin changes only.
COPY backend/requirements*.txt ./backend/
RUN pip install -r backend/requirements.txt

# ── Runtime: slim base + the venv + app code ─────────────────────────────────
FROM python:3.13-slim AS runtime

# Link the GHCR package to this repo (shows under the repo's Packages and lets the repo's Actions
# GITHUB_TOKEN push to it — ADR 0023/0024).
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ"
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.description="DataQ backend (FastAPI API + Celery worker)"
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.licenses="MIT"

ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1

WORKDIR /workspace

# The fully-built venv from the builder (no compilers / apt lists in this layer).
COPY --from=builder /opt/venv /opt/venv

# Application code + tooling config (pyproject is imported for runtime config).
COPY pyproject.toml ./
COPY backend ./backend

# docs/site backs the `get_doc` MCP tool (#1626) — the whole published (public,
# GH-Pages-built) tree copies in for one source of truth, ~1.8MB; the curated
# allowlist actually served lives ONLY in `mcp/docs_catalog.py`, not here.
COPY docs/site ./docs/site

# Run as a dedicated non-root user (#1408): a future RCE through the parser/interpreter surface
# (custom SQL, flat-file content) lands in a privilege-constrained process instead of uid 0.
# /workspace and /opt/venv deliberately STAY root-owned and read-only to this user — the app writes
# nothing there (celery-beat's schedule shelve is pointed at the temp dir in celery_app.py for
# exactly this reason). --create-home because libraries treat $HOME as writable cache space (the
# Snowflake connector's OCSP cache, for one); the uid is >10000 so it can't collide with a host
# uid. Local dev: docker-compose bind-mounts ./backend over /workspace/backend, so a
# restrictive-umask checkout (no world-read) fails imports under uid 10001 — chmod the tree.
RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 dataq
USER 10001

EXPOSE 8000

# Default to the API; the worker overrides `command` (compose / Container App), and the migrate job
# runs `alembic upgrade head`. psycopg2-binary (a wheel) keeps the image apt-free.
CMD ["uvicorn", "backend.app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
--- FRONTEND DOCKERFILE
# DataQ frontend image — build the Vite SPA, serve the static dist via nginx.

# Pin the build stage to the native BUILD platform (amd64 on CI runners) even for an arm64 target
# image: a Vite SPA compiles to architecture-independent static assets.
FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
RUN corepack enable

COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ./
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

COPY . .
RUN pnpm build

FROM nginx:1.27-alpine AS serve
# Link the GHCR package to this repo (shows under the repo's Packages, lets the repo's Actions
# GITHUB_TOKEN push it, and inherits anonymous-pull visibility — ADR 0023, mirrors
# backend/Dockerfile).
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ"
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.description="DataQ frontend (React SPA served by nginx)"
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.licenses="MIT"
COPY --from=build /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
# Template (not a static conf): the nginx entrypoint envsubst's it at startup so
# the API upstream + auth config are runtime-configurable.
COPY nginx.conf.template /etc/nginx/templates/default.conf.template
# Security headers (#1387), `include`d from the template above.
COPY nginx-security-headers.conf /etc/nginx/nginx-security-headers.conf
# Writes the `listen` directives (plain, or TLS when a certificate is configured) before the
# image's own 20-envsubst step.
COPY docker-entrypoint.d/19-dataq-listen.sh /docker-entrypoint.d/19-dataq-listen.sh
# Opt into the nginx image's built-in resolver detection: its 15-local-resolvers.envsh only exports
# ${NGINX_LOCAL_RESOLVERS} (the /etc/resolv.conf nameservers, used by the proxy `resolver`
# directive) when this flag is set.
ENV NGINX_ENTRYPOINT_LOCAL_RESOLVERS=1
# Runtime config env (ADR 0028) — MUST be defined (even if empty) so envsubst always substitutes
# them in /config.js; empty → SPA is unconfigured (fail-closed).
ENV DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM=http://api:8000 \
    DATAQ_AUTH_MODE="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_SCOPE="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_LOGOUT_STYLE="" \
    DATAQ_ORIGIN_SECRET="" \
    DATAQ_CSP_CONNECT_SRC="https:" \
    DATAQ_HSTS="max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" \
    DATAQ_TLS_CERT="" \
    DATAQ_TLS_KEY="" \
    DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM_CA=""
EXPOSE 8080

name: Publish images (GHCR, multi-arch)

# Builds + publishes the BYOL distribution images to GHCR — multi-arch (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64)
# so Apple-Silicon devs pull a native image, not an emulated one (#472).

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: "Extra immutable tag to publish alongside :latest + the commit SHA (e.g. v1.0.0). Blank → just :latest + SHA."
        default: ""
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"
    branches:
      - main
    # NOTE: `paths` is IGNORED for tag pushes — GitHub applies path filters to branch pushes only
    # (github/community discussion #165354 is an open request to make them apply to tags, which is
    # the proof they currently do not). So a vX.Y.Z release ALWAYS publishes regardless of what it
    # touched — verified before this filter was added. Do NOT "fix" this by splitting the workflow.
    paths:
      # Anything that changes what the images CONTAIN…
      - "backend/**"
      - "frontend/**"
      # backend/Dockerfile COPYs this into the image, so it is image content too.
      - "pyproject.toml"
      # …and BOTH halves of the eval contract, each of which docs tell evaluators to fetch from
      # `main`: the compose file, and the env template.
      - "docker-compose.ghcr.yml"
      - ".env.app.example"
      # …plus this workflow, so a change to how images are built takes effect.
      - ".github/workflows/publish-images.yml"

concurrency:
  # Keyed by ref TYPE, not one global group.
  group: publish-images-${{ github.ref_type }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

# GITHUB_TOKEN needs packages:write to push to the repo-linked GHCR packages
# (ADR 0023). No Azure/registry credential is involved.
permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  # Lowercase owner — GHCR paths are case-sensitive and must be lowercase.
  OWNER: theurgicduke771

jobs:
  publish:
    name: Build + push ${{ matrix.name }} (amd64 + arm64)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          # Backend build context is the repo ROOT (the app imports as the
          # top-level `backend.app.*` package — see backend/Dockerfile).
          - name: backend
            dockerfile: backend/Dockerfile
            context: .
          # Frontend build context is frontend/ (its Dockerfile COPYs from there).
          - name: frontend
            dockerfile: frontend/Dockerfile
            context: frontend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # QEMU provides the arm64 emulation the amd64 runner needs to build the
      # non-native platform; buildx drives the multi-platform build + manifest.
      - uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Compute image tags
        id: tags
        # Untrusted inputs come in via env (never interpolated into the script body) so a dispatch
        # `tag` value can't inject shell — IMAGE_NAME is the static matrix name.
        env:
          IMAGE_NAME: ${{ matrix.name }}
          INPUT_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          image="${REGISTRY}/${OWNER}/dataq-${IMAGE_NAME}"
          # The moving stable pointer + a per-commit tag.
          sha_tag="${GITHUB_SHA}"
          if [ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" = "branch" ]; then
            # `/` is legal in a branch name and illegal in a Docker tag.
            sha_tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME//\//-}-${GITHUB_SHA}"
          fi
          tags="${image}:latest"$'\n'"${image}:${sha_tag}"
          # On a release-tag push, github.ref_name is the tag (vX.Y.Z); on a
          # manual run, the optional `tag` input. Publish it as a third tag.
          extra="${INPUT_TAG}"
          if [ -z "$extra" ] && [ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" = "tag" ]; then
            extra="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          fi
          # Validate the extra tag against Docker's tag grammar (alphanumerics +
          # _.- , ≤128 chars, no leading separator) before it reaches the ref.
          if [ -n "$extra" ] && ! printf '%s' "$extra" | grep -Eq '^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,127}$'; then
            echo "::error::Invalid image tag '${extra}' — must match Docker's tag grammar."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -n "$extra" ]; then
            tags="${tags}"$'\n'"${image}:${extra}"
          fi
          echo "Publishing tags:"; echo "$tags"
          # Multi-line output for the build-push-action `tags:` list.
          {
            echo "tags<<EOF"
            echo "$tags"
            echo "EOF"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Build + push (multi-arch)
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: ${{ matrix.context }}
          file: ${{ matrix.dockerfile }}
          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.tags.outputs.tags }}
          # Attestations off: keep the published manifest a plain multi-arch index (no extra
          # unknown/attestation entries) so anonymous ACA/compose pulls resolve cleanly.
          provenance: false
          # Layer cache, added with the per-merge trigger (#1057): this build is now paid on every
          # qualifying merge rather than on the occasional dispatch.
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=${{ matrix.name }}
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=${{ matrix.name }}
--- PUBLISH CLIENT
name: Publish dataq-client

# Attaches the Python client's wheel and sdist to the GitHub Release for a release tag — never a
# branch or a fork build. The package is not published to PyPI; users install the wheel from the
# release, or the latest from main (see packages/dataq-client/README.md).
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  publish:
    name: Build dataq-client and attach it to the release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write  # create the release if needed, and upload its assets
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"

      - name: The tag is the package version
        # The client is versioned with the server it was generated from.
        run: |
          version=$(python -c "import tomllib; print(tomllib.load(open('packages/dataq-client/pyproject.toml','rb'))['project']['version'])")
          if [ "v$version" != "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" ]; then
            echo "::error::tag $GITHUB_REF_NAME does not match dataq-client $version"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Install tooling
        run: pip install -r packages/dataq-client/requirements-dev.txt

      - name: The committed client matches the spec
        run: python scripts/generate-dataq-client.py --check

      - name: Build
        run: python -m build packages/dataq-client --outdir dist

      - name: Attach to the GitHub Release
        # Adds the files to the tag's release. When the tag has none yet, creates it as a DRAFT —
        # nobody is notified of placeholder notes; the maintainer fills in the notes and publishes
        # it (the release checklist). A create that loses a race with a hand-made release falls
        # back to uploading to that one. --clobber makes a re-run idempotent.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if ! gh release view "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --draft --verify-tag --title "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" \
              --notes "Draft: add the curated notes, then publish." \
              || gh release view "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" >/dev/null
          fi
          gh release upload "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" dist/* --clobber

python-client:
    name: Python client (dataq-client) — drift, types, tests, build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip

      - name: Install the package and its tooling
        run: |
          pip install -r packages/dataq-client/requirements-dev.txt
          pip install -e packages/dataq-client

      - name: Generated client matches the committed OpenAPI spec
        # The spec itself is checked against the app in backend-test; a route change must
        # regenerate both (scripts/generate-dataq-client.py).
        run: python scripts/generate-dataq-client.py --check

      - name: Types (hand-written layer)
        run: mypy --config-file packages/dataq-client/pyproject.toml packages/dataq-client/src/dataq_client/client.py packages/dataq-client/src/dataq_client/cli.py

      - name: Tests
        run: pytest -c packages/dataq-client/pyproject.toml -q -p no:cacheprovider packages/dataq-client/tests

      - name: Runtime licences (no strong copyleft or source-available)
        run: python packages/dataq-client/scripts/check_licences.py

      - name: Build the wheel
        run: python -m build --wheel packages/dataq-client --outdir /tmp/dist

  backend-audit:
    name: Backend — dependency audit (pip-audit)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip

      - name: Install pip-audit
        run: pip install pip-audit==2.10.0

      - name: pip-audit (full runtime + test surface)
        # Synchronous CVE gate over the entire runtime + test dependency tree (single source:
        # requirements-dev.txt) + transitive deps, against the PyPI/OSV advisory DB.
        run: |
          # CVE-2026-49265 is in oauthlib's authorization-server PKCE check, which DataQ never runs;
          # databricks-sql-connector pins oauthlib<4.0.0, so the fix can't be installed yet (#2260).
          audit() {
            pip-audit -r backend/requirements-dev.txt --ignore-vuln CVE-2026-49265 \
              && pip-audit -r packages/dataq-client/requirements-dev.txt
          }
          for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
            if audit; then
              exit 0
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" -lt 4 ]; then
              echo "::warning::pip-audit attempt $attempt failed (likely a transient PyPI/OSV 5xx) — retrying in $((attempt * 15))s"
              sleep $((attempt * 15))
            fi
          done
          echo "::error::pip-audit failed after 4 attempts — a real CVE or a persistent PyPI/OSV outage (see log above)"
          exit 1

  backend-test:

content.content:
"""Fail if anything dataq-client installs at runtime is strong-copyleft or source-available.

DataQ ships MIT (ADR 0031); the client is a separate distribution users install into their own
environments, so its runtime tree gets the same check. Walks the installed dependency closure.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.metadata as metadata
import re
import sys

# Both licence spellings: SPDX (`GPL-3.0-only`, `AGPL-3.0`) and the classifiers (`GNU General
# Public License v3 (GPLv3)`, `GNU Affero General Public License v3`). LGPL (the Lesser/Library
# licence) is weak copyleft and allowed with notices, so it is excluded by look-behind.
FORBIDDEN = re.compile(
    r"(?<![A-Za-z])A?GPL|Affero"
    r"|(?<!Lesser )(?<!Library )General Public License"
    r"|SSPL|Server Side Public|BUSL|Business Source|Elastic License|Commons Clause",
    re.I,
)


def _licence(dist: metadata.PackageMetadata) -> str:
    expression = dist.get("License-Expression")
    classifiers = [c for c in dist.get_all("Classifier") or [] if c.startswith("License ::")]
    return expression or "; ".join(classifiers) or (dist.get("License") or "")[:120]


def _closure(root: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    seen: dict[str, str] = {}
    pending = [root]
    while pending:
        name = pending.pop()
        key = name.lower().replace("_", "-")
        if key in seen:
            continue
        try:
            dist = metadata.metadata(name)
        except metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
            continue
        seen[key] = _licence(dist)
        for requirement in metadata.requires(name) or []:
            if "extra ==" in requirement:
                continue
            pending.append(re.split(r"[\s;<>=!~\[]", requirement, maxsplit=1)[0])
    return seen


def main() -> int:
    tree = _closure("dataq-client")
    bad = {n: lic for n, lic in tree.items() if FORBIDDEN.search(lic)}
    unknown = [n for n, lic in tree.items() if not lic.strip()]
    for name, lic in sorted(tree.items()):
        print(f"{name}: {lic or '(none declared)'}")
    if bad or unknown:
        print(f"forbidden: {bad}  undeclared: {unknown}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

--- script style
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Block ADR/issue/PR references from user-visible frontend strings.

An end user has no use for "(ADR 0038)" or "(#1186)" next to a tooltip — they can't
look either up, and the number is meaningless without repo access. That context
belongs in the PR description and the commit, not in a string a Tag/Tooltip/Alert/
form-field renders on screen.

Comments are a different thing entirely and are NOT in scope here — a `//` line, a
`/** JSDoc */` block, and a `{/* JSX */}` block explaining WHY some UI behaves a
certain way are exactly what CONTRIBUTING wants, and betterleaks-style blanket
banning of "#123" would make every honest code comment illegal. So this script
tracks comment state per line (single-line `//`, block `/* ... */`, which is also
how a JSX comment is written) and only flags a match sitting in actual code — a
string literal, template literal, or JSX text — which is what a browser can render.
The comment tracker is purely state-machine-driven (block-open/close spans a line
boundary correctly); it deliberately does NOT also special-case lines starting with
`*`, because that would silently skip real code that happens to start with an
asterisk after leading whitespace.

## The enclosing-parens requirement

Every real reference this script was written to catch — every ADR/issue/PR mention
found across this entire codebase, comments included — is written wrapped in `(...)`
(`"a coverage gap (ADR 0038)"`, `"(#754/#826)"`). A bare `#NNN` with no parens is far
more likely to be ordinary product copy — a batch, run, row or order number DataQ's
own domain produces plenty of ("Batch #4521 processed") — than a dropped ticket
reference, and an unquoted CSS hex color inside a template-literal style block
(`color: #333;`) is never parenthesized either. So a match only counts when it sits
inside an enclosing, unclosed `(` ... `)` pair on the same line; this is a stricter,
evidence-based version of the plain digit-boundary check the earlier draft used
(which false-flagged CSS hex colors and non-ADR numeric UI copy) and needs no
separate hex-color special case.

`console.*` calls and `data-testid` attribute values are also out of scope: neither
reaches the browser's rendered output (a devtools warning and a test hook,
respectively, not something a user reads), so a ticket reference there — however
questionable a practice — isn't the defect this hook exists to catch.

This is a heuristic, not a parser: a `//` inside a string literal (e.g. a URL) is
treated as a comment starting early, which trades a rare false negative for never
false-flagging a legitimate comment. Good enough for a hook whose job is to catch
the common case before it ships, not to be a TypeScript AST.

Deliberate exceptions take an inline `frontend-ui-ok:` pragma **with a reason**, on
the line or the one above it.

Usage: `check-frontend-no-ticket-refs.py [files...]` — no args means every tracked
file under frontend/src. This same invocation (no args) is also what re-runs the
check as a CI backstop, independent of whether pre-commit ran locally.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

PRAGMA = "frontend-ui-ok:"

SCAN_PREFIX = "frontend/src/"
SCAN_SUFFIXES = (".ts", ".tsx")
# Tests render nothing to a real user.
SKIP_SUFFIXES = (".test.ts", ".test.tsx", ".spec.ts", ".spec.tsx")

# Lines whose string content never reaches a browser's rendered output.
NON_RENDERED_MARKERS = (
    "console.log(",
    "console.warn(",
    "console.error(",
    "console.debug(",
    "console.info(",
    "data-testid=",
)

ADR_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\bADR[- ]?\d{2,4}\b", re.IGNORECASE)
# Issue/PR shorthand ("#1186"). A trailing hex-digit or another digit means it's
# not a bare decimal ticket number — bail before the boundary.
TICKET_PATTERN = re.compile(r"#\d{3,5}(?![0-9a-fA-F])")


def _tracked_files() -> list[str]:
    # Literal argv (ruff S603 wants every element provably static, not just constant).
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["/usr/bin/env", "git", "ls-files", "frontend/src/"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return out.stdout.split()


def _scannable(path: str) -> bool:
    if not path.startswith(SCAN_PREFIX):
        return False
    if not path.endswith(SCAN_SUFFIXES):
        return False
    if path.endswith(SKIP_SUFFIXES):
        return False
    return True


def _enclosed_in_parens(text: str, start: int, end: int) -> bool:
    """True when `text[start:end]` sits inside an unclosed `(` ... `)` pair —
    see the module docstring for why this is the scope-narrowing rule."""
    before = text[:start]
    last_open = before.rfind("(")
    if last_open == -1 or ")" in before[last_open:]:
        return False
    after = text[end:]
    first_close = after.find(")")
    if first_close == -1 or "(" in after[:first_close]:
        return False
    return True


def _code_spans(line: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return the substrings of `line` that are NOT inside a comment, given the
    line is not a continuation of an already-open block comment (caller tracks
    that). A `//` or `/*` inside a string literal is not distinguished from a
    real comment start — see module docstring."""
    spans = []
    i = 0
    n = len(line)
    while i < n:
        slash_slash = line.find("//", i)
        slash_star = line.find("/*", i)
        if slash_slash == -1 and slash_star == -1:
            spans.append(line[i:])
            break
        if slash_slash != -1 and (slash_star == -1 or slash_slash < slash_star):
            spans.append(line[i:slash_slash])
            break  # rest of the line is a line comment
        # block comment opens first
        spans.append(line[i:slash_star])
        close = line.find("*/", slash_star + 2)
        if close == -1:
            return spans  # stays open past this line; caller handles continuation
        i = close + 2
    return spans


def scan(paths: list[str]) -> list[tuple[str, int, str, str]]:
    findings: list[tuple[str, int, str, str]] = []
    for path in paths:
        if not _scannable(path):
            continue
        p = Path(path)
        if not p.is_file():
            continue
        try:
            lines = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
            continue
        in_block_comment = False
        for i, raw_line in enumerate(lines, 1):
            if PRAGMA in raw_line or (i >= 2 and PRAGMA in lines[i - 2]):
                continue
            if any(marker in raw_line for marker in NON_RENDERED_MARKERS):
                continue
            line = raw_line
            if in_block_comment:
                close = line.find("*/")
                if close == -1:
                    continue  # whole line still inside the block comment
                line = line[close + 2 :]
                in_block_comment = False
            for span in _code_spans(line):
                for pattern, label in (
                    (ADR_PATTERN, "ADR reference"),
                    (TICKET_PATTERN, "issue/PR reference"),
                ):
                    for m in pattern.finditer(span):
                        if not _enclosed_in_parens(span, m.start(), m.end()):
                            continue
                        findings.append((path, i, label, m.group(0)))
            # Did this line open a block comment that stays open past it?
            last_open = line.rfind("/*")
            last_close = line.rfind("*/")
            if last_open != -1 and (last_close == -1 or last_close < last_open):
                in_block_comment = True
    return findings


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    args = argv[1:]
    paths = args if args else _tracked_files()
    findings = scan(paths)
    if not findings:
        return 0

    print("Frontend UI-text check FAILED — ADR/issue/PR references reach a rendered string:\n")
    for path, line, label, hit in findings:
        print(f"  {path}:{line}  [{label}]  {hit!r}")
    print(
        "\nAn ADR/issue/PR number is meaningless to a user with no repo access — that context\n"
        "belongs in the PR description and commit message, not in a Tooltip/Alert/label/form-\n"
        "field string. Fix one of these ways:\n"
        "  • drop the parenthetical/reference from the user-facing string;\n"
        "  • if this really is a comment the scanner misread (e.g. an unusual multi-line JSX\n"
        f"    comment shape), add `{PRAGMA} <reason>` on the line or the one above."
    )
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))

--- deploy README pre-deploy
## Pre-deploy checklist

Confirm the change is *ready and green* before you push it to prod:

- [ ] **Everything intended is merged to `main`** and you're deploying that known SHA (blank
  `image_tag` → the immutable commit SHA).
- [ ] **CI is fully green** on that SHA — lint, format, type-check, **all unit + integration
  tests**, the security scans (Bandit / CodeQL / secret-scan / dependency-audit), and the
  frontend E2E. The local verification battery (the same gate) passes too — don't let CI be
  the first feedback loop.
- [ ] **Docs are up to date** for what's shipping — `CLAUDE.md` §13 headline + `docs/progress.md`
  ticked; an **ADR** for any significant decision; the **env-var reference** + this deploy
  guide for any new config; and **user docs** for any new user-facing feature.
- [ ] **DB migrations are safe** — additive/backward-compatible (nullable `ADD COLUMN` / new
  table; no `DROP`/rename/`NOT NULL`-without-default in the same PR as the code that needs
  it), `upgrade` **and** `downgrade` tested locally. The workflow runs `alembic upgrade head`
  **before** rolling the apps, so old code never sees a missing column — you just confirm the
  revision is safe. *Note:* an `ALTER` on a hot table (`runs` / `results` / `pipeline_runs`)
  can block on a live-worker lock and hang the migrate job (#605); recovery + root-cause
  hardening are in [#708](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/708).
- [ ] **Migration-specific pre-deploy steps have been run.** Some revisions need a manual step
  against the live database *before* the migrate job runs, and that step lives in the
  **migration's own docstring** — not here, because it is revision-specific and would rot if
  duplicated. Before deploying, list the revisions that are pending on prod
  (`alembic current` vs `alembic heads`) and read each one's docstring in
  `backend/alembic/versions/` for a **`MANDATORY PRE-DEPLOY`** section; run what it says and
  confirm the result is clean. First instance: **`7d25617cfaf0`** (users nullable
  `aad_object_id` + unique `lower(email)`, #735) requires a duplicate-email audit — if it
  finds duplicates, the index creation fails and the migrate job aborts, so resolve them
  first.
- [ ] **Config + secrets are in place** — the required GitHub env/vars and Key Vault secrets
  (see the [prerequisites](#before-you-deploy-production-prerequisites) above), especially any
  new key this release reads.

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

rows = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())
print(len(rows), "packages; keys:", sorted(rows[0].keys()))
counts = collections.Counter(r["License"] for r in rows)
for lic, n in counts.most_common():
    print(f"{n:4d}  {lic!r}")
print("--- UNKNOWN / odd")
for r in rows:
    lic = r["License"]
    if lic == "UNKNOWN" or any(w in lic for w in ("GPL", "UNKNOWN", "Other", "Dual", ";")):
        print(r["Name"], r["Version"], repr(lic), "| file:", r.get("LicenseFile"), "| notice:", r.get("NoticeFile"))
print("--- no licence text")
for r in rows:
    if not r.get("LicenseText") or r.get("LicenseText") == "UNKNOWN":
        print(r["Name"], r["Version"], repr(r["License"]))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Dependency licence gate + THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES generator (CONTRIBUTING rule 40, ADR 0031).

    check-licenses.py backend  [--requirements FILE] [--notices OUT.md]
    check-licenses.py frontend [--prod]
    check-licenses.py all                      # backend (requirements-dev.txt) + frontend (whole tree)

backend: walks the installed closure of the requirements file (the interpreter running this
script must be the one the file was installed into) and reads each distribution's licence
metadata + bundled LICENSE / NOTICE files. frontend: `pnpm licenses list --json` over the
lockfile. A dependency whose licence is not on the allowlist — or is unknown — fails, unless
scripts/licenses/overrides.toml records a reviewed override with evidence. The backend image
build runs this with --notices, so a violation also fails the build.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import importlib.metadata as metadata
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tomllib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from packaging.requirements import InvalidRequirement, Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OVERRIDES = ROOT / "scripts" / "licenses" / "overrides.toml"
FRONTEND = ROOT / "frontend"

ALLOWED = {
    "MIT",
    "MIT-0",
    "X11",
    "BSD",
    "BSD-2-Clause",
    "BSD-3-Clause",
    "0BSD",
    "Apache-2.0",
    "ISC",
    "PSF-2.0",
    "Python-2.0",
    "MPL-2.0",
    "LGPL",
    "LGPL-2.1",
    "LGPL-2.1-only",
    "LGPL-2.1-or-later",
    "LGPL-3.0",
    "LGPL-3.0-only",
    "LGPL-3.0-or-later",
    "Unlicense",
    "Zlib",
    "CC0-1.0",
    "CC-BY-4.0",
    "BlueOak-1.0.0",
    "OFL-1.1",
    "HPND",
}

FORBIDDEN = re.compile(
    r"(?<![A-Za-z])A?GPL(?!.*Lesser)|Affero|SSPL|Server Side Public|BUSL|Business Source"
    r"|Elastic|Commons.Clause|Artistic|CC-BY-NC|NonCommercial|Proprietary|UNKNOWN",
    re.I,
)

# Trove classifiers and free-text spellings → SPDX ids.
_SPELLINGS = {
    "mit license": "MIT",
    "mit": "MIT",
    "mit-0": "MIT-0",
    "apache software license": "Apache-2.0",
    "apache license 2.0": "Apache-2.0",
    "apache license, version 2.0": "Apache-2.0",
    "apache 2.0": "Apache-2.0",
    "apache-2": "Apache-2.0",
    "apache": "Apache-2.0",
    "bsd license": "BSD",
    "bsd": "BSD",
    "3-clause bsd license": "BSD-3-Clause",
    "new bsd license": "BSD-3-Clause",
    "bsd 3-clause": "BSD-3-Clause",
    "bsd-3": "BSD-3-Clause",
    "bsd 2-clause": "BSD-2-Clause",
    "simplified bsd": "BSD-2-Clause",
    "isc license (iscl)": "ISC",
    "isc": "ISC",
    "python software foundation license": "PSF-2.0",
    "psf": "PSF-2.0",
    "mozilla public license 2.0 (mpl 2.0)": "MPL-2.0",
    "mpl 2.0": "MPL-2.0",
    "mpl-2.0": "MPL-2.0",
    "the unlicense (unlicense)": "Unlicense",
    "unlicense": "Unlicense",
    "gnu library or lesser general public license (lgpl)": "LGPL",
    "gnu lesser general public license v3 (lgplv3)": "LGPL-3.0",
    "gnu lesser general public license v2 or later (lgplv2+)": "LGPL-2.1-or-later",
    "gnu lesser general public license v3 or later (lgplv3+)": "LGPL-3.0-or-later",
    "zlib/libpng license": "Zlib",
    "zlib": "Zlib",
    "cc0 1.0 universal (cc0 1.0) public domain dedication": "CC0-1.0",
    "freely distributable": "Freely-Distributable",
}


def normalise(atom: str) -> str:
    text = atom.strip().strip('"').rstrip(".")
    text = re.sub(r"^(license\s*::\s*)?(osi approved\s*::\s*)?", "", text, flags=re.I)
    return _SPELLINGS.get(text.lower(), text)


def _tokens(expression: str) -> list[str]:
    # Classifier lists arrive "; "-joined — several licences the user picks between, so `;` = OR.
    expression = expression.replace(";", " OR ")
    return [t for t in re.split(r"(\(|\)|\s+(?:AND|OR|WITH)\s+)", expression, flags=re.I) if t.strip()]


def allowed(expression: str, allow: set[str] = ALLOWED) -> bool:
    """Evaluate an SPDX-style expression: an OR needs one allowed side, an AND needs both."""
    tokens = _tokens(expression)
    pos = 0

    def parse_or() -> bool:
        nonlocal pos
        value = parse_and()
        while pos < len(tokens) and tokens[pos].strip().upper() == "OR":
            pos += 1
            value = parse_and() or value
        return value

    def parse_and() -> bool:
        nonlocal pos
        value = parse_atom()
        while pos < len(tokens) and tokens[pos].strip().upper() == "AND":
            pos += 1
            value = parse_atom() and value
        return value

    def parse_atom() -> bool:
        nonlocal pos
        if pos >= len(tokens):
            return False
        token = tokens[pos]
        pos += 1
        if token == "(":
            value = parse_or()
            pos += 1  # ')'
            return value
        if pos < len(tokens) and tokens[pos].strip().upper() == "WITH":
            pos += 2  # exceptions (e.g. LLVM-exception) do not change the base grant
        return normalise(token) in allow

    return bool(tokens) and parse_or()


@dataclass
class Package:
    name: str
    version: str
    licence: str
    homepage: str = ""
    author: str = ""
    texts: list[tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    override: str = ""


def load_overrides(path: Path = OVERRIDES) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:
    if not path.exists():
        return {}
    data = tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    out: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
    for section in ("backend", "frontend"):
        for name, entry in data.get(section, {}).items():
            for key in ("license", "evidence", "reason"):
                if not entry.get(key):
                    raise SystemExit(f"{path}: [{section}.{name!r}] needs `{key}`")
            out[f"{section}:{canonicalize_name(name)}"] = entry
    return out


def apply_override(pkg: Package, side: str, overrides: dict[str, dict[str, str]]) -> None:
    entry = overrides.get(f"{side}:{canonicalize_name(pkg.name)}")
    if entry is None:
        return
    if entry.get("version") and entry["version"] != pkg.version:
        return
    pkg.override = f"declared {pkg.licence!r}; {entry['reason']} — {entry['evidence']}"
    pkg.licence = entry["license"]


# ── backend ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def read_requirements(path: Path) -> list[Requirement]:
    out: list[Requirement] = []
    for raw in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = raw.split("#", 1)[0].strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        if line.startswith("-r "):
            out.extend(read_requirements(path.parent / line[3:].strip()))
            continue
        if line.startswith("-"):
            continue
        try:
            out.append(Requirement(line))
        except InvalidRequirement as exc:
            raise SystemExit(f"{path}: cannot parse {line!r}: {exc}") from exc
    return out


def _licence_of(dist: metadata.Distribution) -> str:
    meta = dist.metadata
    expression = meta.get("License-Expression")
    if expression:
        return expression
    classifiers = [c for c in meta.get_all("Classifier") or [] if c.startswith("License ::")]
    if classifiers:
        return "; ".join(normalise(c) for c in classifiers)
    free_text = (meta.get("License") or "").strip()
    if free_text and "\n" not in free_text and len(free_text) < 80:
        return free_text
    return "UNKNOWN"


_TEXT_FILE = re.compile(r"^(LICEN[CS]E|COPYING|NOTICE|AUTHORS)", re.I)


def _texts_of(dist: metadata.Distribution) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    out: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for entry in dist.files or []:
        parts = entry.parts
        if len(parts) < 2 or not parts[0].endswith(".dist-info"):
            continue
        if parts[1] == "licenses" or _TEXT_FILE.match(parts[-1]):
            if _TEXT_FILE.match(parts[-1]) or parts[1] == "licenses":
                try:
                    out.append((parts[-1], dist.read_text(str(entry)) or ""))
                except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
                    continue
    return sorted(out)


def _homepage(dist: metadata.Distribution) -> str:
    meta = dist.metadata
    for url in meta.get_all("Project-URL") or []:
        label, _, target = url.partition(",")
        if label.strip().lower() in ("homepage", "source", "repository", "source code"):
            return target.strip()
    return meta.get("Home-page") or ""


def backend_closure(requirements: list[Requirement]) -> list[Package]:
    pending: list[tuple[str, frozenset[str]]] = [(r.name, frozenset(r.extras)) for r in requirements]
    seen: dict[str, Package] = {}
    extras_seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    missing: list[str] = []
    while pending:
        name, extras = pending.pop()
        key = canonicalize_name(name)
        try:
            dist = metadata.distribution(key)
        except metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
            missing.append(key)
            continue
        if key not in seen:
            seen[key] = Package(
                name=dist.metadata["Name"],
                version=dist.version,
                licence=_licence_of(dist),
                homepage=_homepage(dist),
                author=dist.metadata.get("Author") or dist.metadata.get("Author-email") or "",
                texts=_texts_of(dist),
            )
        for extra in sorted(extras | {""}):
            if (key, extra) in extras_seen:
                continue
            extras_seen.add((key, extra))
            for spec in dist.requires or []:
                req = Requirement(spec)
                if req.marker is not None and not req.marker.evaluate({"extra": extra}):
                    continue
                pending.append((req.name, frozenset(req.extras)))
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit(
            "not installed in this interpreter (run the check with the environment the "
            f"requirements were installed into): {sorted(set(missing))}"
        )
    return sorted(seen.values(), key=lambda p: p.name.lower())


# ── frontend ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def frontend_packages(prod: bool) -> list[Package]:
    cmd = ["pnpm", "licenses", "list", "--json"] + (["--prod"] if prod else [])
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=FRONTEND, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise SystemExit(f"{' '.join(cmd)} failed:\n{result.stderr}")
    out: list[Package] = []
    for licence, entries in json.loads(result.stdout).items():
        for entry in entries:
            out.append(
                Package(
                    name=entry["name"],
                    version=", ".join(entry.get("versions") or []),
                    licence=entry.get("license") or licence or "UNKNOWN",
                    homepage=entry.get("homepage") or "",
                    author=entry.get("author") or "",
                )
            )
    return sorted(out, key=lambda p: p.name.lower())


# ── report ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def violations(packages: list[Package]) -> list[Package]:
    return [p for p in packages if not allowed(p.licence)]


def render_notices(title: str, packages: list[Package]) -> str:
    lines = [
        f"# Third-party notices — {title}",
        "",
        "DataQ is MIT-licensed. This image bundles the following third-party packages under their",
        "own licences; the full licence texts and Apache NOTICE contents shipped with each package",
        "are reproduced below. Generated at build time by `scripts/check-licenses.py`.",
        "",
        f"{len(packages)} packages.",
        "",
        "| Package | Version | Licence | Homepage |",
        "|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for p in packages:
        note = " (reviewed override: see below)" if p.override else ""
        lines.append(f"| {p.name} | {p.version} | {p.licence}{note} | {p.homepage} |")
    lines += ["", "## Licence texts", ""]
    for p in packages:
        lines += [f"### {p.name} {p.version} — {p.licence}", ""]
        if p.author:
            lines += [f"Author: {p.author}", ""]
        if p.override:
            lines += [f"Licence override: {p.override}", ""]
        if not p.texts:
            where = p.homepage or "the project's source distribution"
            lines += [f"No licence text is shipped in the distribution; see {where}.", ""]
        for filename, text in p.texts:
            lines += [f"#### {filename}", "", "```text", text.rstrip("\n"), "```", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def check(side: str, packages: list[Package], overrides: dict[str, dict[str, str]]) -> int:
    for p in packages:
        apply_override(p, side, overrides)
    bad = violations(packages)
    print(f"{side}: {len(packages)} packages, {len(bad)} licence violation(s)")
    for p in bad:
        kind = "forbidden" if FORBIDDEN.search(p.licence) else "not on the allowlist"
        print(f"  {p.name} {p.version}: {p.licence!r} — {kind}")
    if bad:
        print(
            "A strong-copyleft or source-available dependency needs an ADR-level exception (rule 40);\n"
            "a package whose metadata misstates a known-permissive licence needs a reviewed entry in\n"
            f"{OVERRIDES.relative_to(ROOT)} with the evidence URL."
        )
    return 1 if bad else 0


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("side", choices=["backend", "frontend", "all"])
    parser.add_argument("--requirements", type=Path, default=ROOT / "backend" / "requirements-dev.txt")
    parser.add_argument("--notices", type=Path, help="backend: write THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md here")
    parser.add_argument("--prod", action="store_true", help="frontend: runtime dependencies only")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv[1:])
    overrides = load_overrides()
    rc = 0
    if args.side in ("backend", "all"):
        packages = backend_closure(read_requirements(args.requirements))
        rc |= check("backend", packages, overrides)
        if args.notices and rc == 0:
            args.notices.write_text(render_notices("DataQ backend", packages), encoding="utf-8")
            print(f"wrote {args.notices}")
    if args.side in ("frontend", "all"):
        rc |= check("frontend", frontend_packages(args.prod), overrides)
    return rc


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

    "LGPL-3.0",
    "LGPL-3.0-only",
    "LGPL-3.0-or-later",
    "Unlicense",
    "Zlib",
    "CC0-1.0",
    "CC-BY-4.0",
    "BlueOak-1.0.0",
    "OFL-1.1",
    "HPND",
}

FORBIDDEN = re.compile(
    r"(?<![A-Za-z])A?GPL(?!.*Lesser)|Affero|SSPL|Server Side Public|BUSL|Business Source"
    r"|Elastic|Commons.Clause|Artistic|CC-BY-NC|NonCommercial|Proprietary|UNKNOWN",
    re.I,
)

# Trove classifiers and free-text spellings → SPDX ids.
_SPELLINGS = {
    "mit license": "MIT",
    "mit": "MIT",
    "mit-0": "MIT-0",
    "apache software license": "Apache-2.0",
    "apache license 2.0": "Apache-2.0",
    "apache license, version 2.0": "Apache-2.0",
    "apache 2.0": "Apache-2.0",
    "apache-2": "Apache-2.0",
    "apache": "Apache-2.0",
    "bsd license": "BSD",
    "bsd": "BSD",
    "3-clause bsd license": "BSD-3-Clause",
    "new bsd license": "BSD-3-Clause",
    "bsd 3-clause": "BSD-3-Clause",
    "bsd-3": "BSD-3-Clause",
    "bsd 2-clause": "BSD-2-Clause",
    "simplified bsd": "BSD-2-Clause",
    "isc license (iscl)": "ISC",
    "isc": "ISC",
    "python software foundation license": "PSF-2.0",
    "psf": "PSF-2.0",
    "mozilla public license 2.0 (mpl 2.0)": "MPL-2.0",
    "mpl 2.0": "MPL-2.0",
    "mpl-2.0": "MPL-2.0",
    "the unlicense (unlicense)": "Unlicense",
    "unlicense": "Unlicense",
    "gnu library or lesser general public license (lgpl)": "LGPL",
    "gnu lesser general public license v3 (lgplv3)": "LGPL-3.0",
    "gnu lesser general public license v2 or later (lgplv2+)": "LGPL-2.1-or-later",
    "gnu lesser general public license v3 or later (lgplv3+)": "LGPL-3.0-or-later",
    "zlib/libpng license": "Zlib",
    "zlib": "Zlib",
    "cc0 1.0 universal (cc0 1.0) public domain dedication": "CC0-1.0",
    "freely distributable": "Freely-Distributable",
}


def normalise(atom: str) -> str:
    text = atom.strip().strip('"').rstrip(".")
    text = re.sub(r"^(license\s*::\s*)?(osi approved\s*::\s*)?", "", text, flags=re.I)
    return _SPELLINGS.get(text.lower(), text)


def _tokens(expression: str) -> list[str]:
    # Classifier lists arrive "; "-joined — several licences the user picks between, so `;` = OR.
    expression = expression.replace(";", " OR ")
    return [t for t in re.split(r"(\(|\)|\s+(?:AND|OR|WITH)\s+)", expression, flags=re.I) if t.strip()]


def allowed(expression: str, allow: set[str] = ALLOWED) -> bool:
    """Evaluate an SPDX-style expression: an OR needs one allowed side, an AND needs both."""
    tokens = _tokens(expression)
    pos = 0

    def parse_or() -> bool:
        nonlocal pos
        value = parse_and()
        while pos < len(tokens) and tokens[pos].strip().upper() == "OR":
            pos += 1
            value = parse_and() or value
        return value

    def parse_and() -> bool:
        nonlocal pos
        value = parse_atom()
        while pos < len(tokens) and tokens[pos].strip().upper() == "AND":
            pos += 1
            value = parse_atom() and value
        return value

    def parse_atom() -> bool:
        nonlocal pos
        if pos >= len(tokens):
            return False
        token = tokens[pos]
        pos += 1
        if token == "(":
            value = parse_or()
            pos += 1  # ')'
            return value
        if pos < len(tokens) and tokens[pos].strip().upper() == "WITH":
            pos += 2  # exceptions (e.g. LLVM-exception) do not change the base grant
        return normalise(token) in allow

    return bool(tokens) and parse_or()


@dataclass
class Package:
    name: str
    version: str
    licence: str
    homepage: str = ""
    author: str = ""
    texts: list[tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    override: str = ""


def load_overrides(path: Path = OVERRIDES) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:
    if not path.exists():
        return {}
    data = tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    out: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
    for section in ("backend", "frontend"):
        for name, entry in data.get(section, {}).items():
            for key in ("license", "evidence", "reason"):
                if not entry.get(key):
                    raise SystemExit(f"{path}: [{section}.{name!r}] needs `{key}`")
            out[f"{section}:{canonicalize_name(name)}"] = entry
    return out


def apply_override(pkg: Package, side: str, overrides: dict[str, dict[str, str]]) -> None:
    entry = overrides.get(f"{side}:{canonicalize_name(pkg.name)}")
    if entry is None:
        return
    if entry.get("version") and entry["version"] != pkg.version:
        return
    pkg.override = f"declared {pkg.licence!r}; {entry['reason']} — {entry['evidence']}"
    pkg.licence = entry["license"]


# ── backend ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def read_requirements(path: Path) -> list[Requirement]:
    out: list[Requirement] = []
    for raw in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = raw.split("#", 1)[0].strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        if line.startswith("-r "):
            out.extend(read_requirements(path.parent / line[3:].strip()))
            continue
        if line.startswith("-"):
            continue
        try:
            out.append(Requirement(line))
        except InvalidRequirement as exc:
            raise SystemExit(f"{path}: cannot parse {line!r}: {exc}") from exc
    return out


def _licence_of(dist: metadata.Distribution) -> str:
    meta = dist.metadata
    expression = meta.get("License-Expression")
    if expression:
        return expression
    classifiers = [c for c in meta.get_all("Classifier") or [] if c.startswith("License ::")]
    if classifiers:
        return "; ".join(normalise(c) for c in classifiers)
    free_text = (meta.get("License") or "").strip()
    if free_text and "\n" not in free_text and len(free_text) < 80:
        return free_text
    return "UNKNOWN"


_TEXT_FILE = re.compile(r"^(LICEN[CS]E|COPYING|NOTICE|AUTHORS)", re.I)


def _texts_of(dist: metadata.Distribution) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    out: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for entry in dist.files or []:
        parts = entry.parts
        if len(parts) < 2 or not parts[0].endswith(".dist-info"):
            continue
        if parts[1] == "licenses" or _TEXT_FILE.match(parts[-1]):
            if _TEXT_FILE.match(parts[-1]) or parts[1] == "licenses":
                try:
                    out.append((parts[-1], dist.read_text(str(entry)) or ""))
                except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
                    continue
    return sorted(out)


def _homepage(dist: metadata.Distribution) -> str:
    meta = dist.metadata
    for url in meta.get_all("Project-URL") or []:
        label, _, target = url.partition(",")
        if label.strip().lower() in ("homepage", "source", "repository", "source code"):
            return target.strip()
    return meta.get("Home-page") or ""


def backend_closure(requirements: list[Requirement]) -> list[Package]:
    pending: list[tuple[str, frozenset[str]]] = [(r.name, frozenset(r.extras)) for r in requirements]
    seen: dict[str, Package] = {}
    extras_seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    missing: list[str] = []
    while pending:
        name, extras = pending.pop()
        key = canonicalize_name(name)
        try:
            dist = metadata.distribution(key)
        except metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
            missing.append(key)
            continue
        if key not in seen:
            seen[key] = Package(
                name=dist.metadata["Name"],
                version=dist.version,
                licence=_licence_of(dist),
                homepage=_homepage(dist),
                author=dist.metadata.get("Author") or dist.metadata.get("Author-email") or "",
                texts=_texts_of(dist),
            )
        for extra in sorted(extras | {""}):
            if (key, extra) in extras_seen:
                continue
            extras_seen.add((key, extra))
            for spec in dist.requires or []:
                req = Requirement(spec)
                if req.marker is not None and not req.marker.evaluate({"extra": extra}):
                    continue
                pending.append((req.name, frozenset(req.extras)))
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit(
            "not installed in this interpreter (run the check with the environment the "
            f"requirements were installed into): {sorted(set(missing))}"
        )
    return sorted(seen.values(), key=lambda p: p.name.lower())


# ── frontend ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def frontend_packages(prod: bool) -> list[Package]:
    cmd = ["pnpm", "licenses", "list", "--json"] + (["--prod"] if prod else [])
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=FRONTEND, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise SystemExit(f"{' '.join(cmd)} failed:\n{result.stderr}")
    out: list[Package] = []
    for licence, entries in json.loads(result.stdout).items():
        for entry in entries:
            out.append(
                Package(
                    name=entry["name"],
                    version=", ".join(entry.get("versions") or []),
                    licence=entry.get("license") or licence or "UNKNOWN",
                    homepage=entry.get("homepage") or "",
                    author=entry.get("author") or "",
                )
            )
    return sorted(out, key=lambda p: p.name.lower())


# ── report ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def violations(packages: list[Package]) -> list[Package]:
    return [p for p in packages if not allowed(p.licence)]


def render_notices(title: str, packages: list[Package]) -> str:
    lines = [
        f"# Third-party notices — {title}",
        "",
        "DataQ is MIT-licensed. This image bundles the following third-party packages under their",
        "own licences; the full licence texts and Apache NOTICE contents shipped with each package",
        "are reproduced below. Generated at build time by `scripts/check-licenses.py`.",
        "",
        f"{len(packages)} packages.",
        "",
        "| Package | Version | Licence | Homepage |",
        "|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for p in packages:
        note = " (reviewed override: see below)" if p.override else ""
        lines.append(f"| {p.name} | {p.version} | {p.licence}{note} | {p.homepage} |")
    lines += ["", "## Licence texts", ""]
    for p in packages:
        lines += [f"### {p.name} {p.version} — {p.licence}", ""]
        if p.author:
            lines += [f"Author: {p.author}", ""]
        if p.override:
            lines += [f"Licence override: {p.override}", ""]
        if not p.texts:
            where = p.homepage or "the project's source distribution"
            lines += [f"No licence text is shipped in the distribution; see {where}.", ""]
        for filename, text in p.texts:
            lines += [f"#### {filename}", "", "```text", text.rstrip("\n"), "```", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def check(side: str, packages: list[Package], overrides: dict[str, dict[str, str]]) -> int:
    for p in packages:
        apply_override(p, side, overrides)
    bad = violations(packages)
    print(f"{side}: {len(packages)} packages, {len(bad)} licence violation(s)")
    for p in bad:
        kind = "forbidden" if FORBIDDEN.search(p.licence) else "not on the allowlist"
        print(f"  {p.name} {p.version}: {p.licence!r} — {kind}")
    if bad:
        print(
            "A strong-copyleft or source-available dependency needs an ADR-level exception (rule 40);\n"
            "a package whose metadata misstates a known-permissive licence needs a reviewed entry in\n"
            f"{OVERRIDES.relative_to(ROOT)} with the evidence URL."
        )
    return 1 if bad else 0


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("side", choices=["backend", "frontend", "all"])
    parser.add_argument("--requirements", type=Path, default=ROOT / "backend" / "requirements-dev.txt")
    parser.add_argument("--notices", type=Path, help="backend: write THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md here")
    parser.add_argument("--prod", action="store_true", help="frontend: runtime dependencies only")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv[1:])
    overrides = load_overrides()
    rc = 0
    if args.side in ("backend", "all"):
        packages = backend_closure(read_requirements(args.requirements))
        rc |= check("backend", packages, overrides)
        if args.notices and rc == 0:
            args.notices.write_text(render_notices("DataQ backend", packages), encoding="utf-8")
            print(f"wrote {args.notices}")
    if args.side in ("frontend", "all"):
        rc |= check("frontend", frontend_packages(args.prod), overrides)
    return rc


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

# Third-party services & sub-processor disclosure

> **Who this is for:** the organization deploying DataQ (the data **controller** /
> covered entity) and its privacy/security reviewers. DataQ ships as
> **customer-deployed BYOL** (ADR 0013): there is no DataQ-hosted SaaS, so DataQ
> the company holds none of your data and, in the classic GDPR Art 28 sense, has
> **no sub-processors of your data at all**. What a controller still needs from us —
> and cannot produce themselves — is the list below: **every external service the
> software can send data to**, so your own sub-processor register and DPIA can
> name them. Which entries apply to *your* deployment depends on what you enable
> and where you point it.

--- publication rule
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Every doc must make a deliberate publish/don't-publish choice.
Since the docs/site/ split, **location is the decision**: MkDocs' `docs_dir` is
`docs/site/`, so a file publishes if and only if it lives under `docs/site/`.
Internal planning docs sit directly under `docs/` where the site build never
sees them. (Before the split, everything under `docs/` published by default and
an `exclude_docs` allowlist held the internal set — a default that once put the
ops log, with a personal email and a live database server name, on the public
site because nobody *decided* to publish it.)
Two things are still worth guarding:
  1. `docs_dir` must stay `docs/site` — if it silently reverts to `docs`, every
     internal file publishes again. This hook pins it.
  2. A page added under `docs/site/` should be *findable*: either in `nav`, or
     matching PUBLISHED_UNLINKED below (today: ADRs — reachable from prose and
     the ADR index; forty sidebar entries would bury the guides). A page in
     neither is almost always a nav entry someone forgot, so it fails here —
     as an explicit-decision prompt, not a publication risk.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import re
from pathlib import Path
SITE = Path("docs/site")
MKDOCS = Path("mkdocs.yml")
# Published deliberately, but not in the nav. Glob patterns, relative to docs/site/.
PUBLISHED_UNLINKED = ("adr/*.md",)
def _nav_entries(text: str) -> set[str]:
    """Every `*.md` mentioned in the nav block.
    Deliberately a regex over the nav section rather than a YAML parse: mkdocs.yml
    carries mkdocs-material's `!!python/name:` tags, which the safe loader refuses
    (the repo's own check-yaml hook passes `--unsafe` for the same reason).
--- mkdocs redirect block
        feature-matrix.md: reference/feature-matrix.md
        rest-api.md: reference/rest-api.md
        glossary.md: reference/glossary.md
        changelog.md: reference/changelog.md
        mcp-honesty.md: architecture/mcp-honesty.md
        evidence-card.md: architecture/evidence-card.md
        perf-baseline.md: architecture/perf-baseline.md
        contributing.md: architecture/contributing.md
        compliance/sub-processors.md: security/compliance/sub-processors.md
        compliance/dpia-input-sheet.md: security/compliance/dpia-input-sheet.md
        compliance/data-subject-rights-runbook.md: security/compliance/data-subject-rights-runbook.md
        compliance/breach-notification-runbook.md: security/compliance/breach-notification-runbook.md
        compliance/dpa-baa-templates.md: security/compliance/dpa-baa-templates.md
        deployment.md: operate/deployment.md
        deployment-parity.md: operate/deployment-parity.md
        observability.md: operate/observability.md

import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

_SCRIPT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "scripts" / "check-licenses.py"
_SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("check_licenses", _SCRIPT)
assert _SPEC is not None and _SPEC.loader is not None
cl = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_SPEC)
_SPEC.loader.exec_module(cl)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "expression",
    [
        "MIT",
        "MIT License",
        "Apache Software License",
        "Apache-2.0 AND MIT",
        "Apache Software License; BSD License",
        "(MPL-2.0 OR Apache-2.0)",
        "MIT OR GPL-3.0-only",
        "Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception",
        "GNU Library or Lesser General Public License (LGPL)",
        "LGPL-3.0-or-later",
        "Python Software Foundation License",
        "The Unlicense (Unlicense)",
        "BSD-3-Clause AND 0BSD AND MIT AND Zlib AND CC0-1.0",
        "OFL-1.1",
    ],
)
def test_allowed_expressions(expression: str) -> None:
    assert cl.allowed(expression)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "expression",
    [
        "UNKNOWN",
        "",
        "GPL-3.0-only",
        "GNU General Public License v3 (GPLv3)",
        "AGPL-3.0",
        "SSPL-1.0",
        "BUSL-1.1",
        "Elastic-2.0",
        "MIT AND GPL-2.0-only",
        "Artistic License; GNU General Public License (GPL)",
        "Something-Nobody-Reviewed-1.0",
        "Proprietary",
    ],
)
def test_rejected_expressions(expression: str) -> None:
    assert not cl.allowed(expression)


def test_forbidden_pattern_spares_lgpl() -> None:
    assert cl.FORBIDDEN.search("GPL-3.0-only")
    assert cl.FORBIDDEN.search("GNU Affero General Public License v3")
    assert not cl.FORBIDDEN.search("LGPL-3.0-only")
    assert not cl.FORBIDDEN.search("GNU Library or Lesser General Public License (LGPL)")


def _pkg(name: str, licence: str, version: str = "1.0") -> object:
    return cl.Package(name=name, version=version, licence=licence)


def test_check_fails_on_forbidden_and_unknown(capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]) -> None:
    packages = [_pkg("fine", "MIT"), _pkg("copyleft", "GPL-3.0-only"), _pkg("mystery", "UNKNOWN")]
    assert cl.check("backend", packages, {}) == 1
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "copyleft 1.0: 'GPL-3.0-only' — forbidden" in out
    assert "mystery 1.0: 'UNKNOWN' — forbidden" in out
    assert "fine" not in out.split("violation(s)")[1]


def test_check_passes_clean_set() -> None:
    assert cl.check("backend", [_pkg("a", "MIT"), _pkg("b", "BSD License")], {}) == 0


def _overrides(tmp_path: Path, body: str) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:
    path = tmp_path / "overrides.toml"
    path.write_text(body, encoding="utf-8")
    return cl.load_overrides(path)


def test_override_rescues_unknown_metadata_with_evidence(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    overrides = _overrides(
        tmp_path,
        '[backend.My_Pkg]\nlicense = "Apache-2.0"\nevidence = "https://example.test/COPYING"\n'
        'reason = "wheel has no licence metadata"\n',
    )
    pkg = _pkg("my-pkg", "UNKNOWN")
    assert cl.check("backend", [pkg], overrides) == 0
    assert pkg.licence == "Apache-2.0"
    assert "declared 'UNKNOWN'" in pkg.override and "https://example.test/COPYING" in pkg.override


def test_override_is_side_and_version_scoped(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    overrides = _overrides(
        tmp_path,
        '[frontend.pkg]\nlicense = "MIT"\nevidence = "https://example.test"\nreason = "r"\n'
        'version = "2.0"\n',
    )
    assert cl.check("backend", [_pkg("pkg", "UNKNOWN")], overrides) == 1
    assert cl.check("frontend", [_pkg("pkg", "UNKNOWN", version="1.0")], overrides) == 1
    assert cl.check("frontend", [_pkg("pkg", "UNKNOWN", version="2.0")], overrides) == 0


def test_override_cannot_admit_a_forbidden_licence(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    overrides = _overrides(
        tmp_path,
        '[backend.pkg]\nlicense = "GPL-3.0-only"\nevidence = "https://example.test"\nreason = "r"\n',
    )
    assert cl.check("backend", [_pkg("pkg", "UNKNOWN")], overrides) == 1


def test_override_without_evidence_is_refused(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="needs `evidence`"):
        _overrides(tmp_path, '[backend.pkg]\nlicense = "MIT"\nreason = "r"\n')


def test_committed_overrides_file_is_well_formed() -> None:
    overrides = cl.load_overrides()
    for key, entry in overrides.items():
        assert cl.allowed(entry["license"]), key
        assert entry["evidence"].startswith("https://"), key


def test_backend_closure_follows_extras_and_requirement_includes(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    child = tmp_path / "child.txt"
    child.write_text("pytest==9.1.1  # comment\n", encoding="utf-8")
    parent = tmp_path / "parent.txt"
    parent.write_text("-r child.txt\n\n# only a comment\ncelery[redis]\n", encoding="utf-8")
    names = {p.name.lower() for p in cl.backend_closure(cl.read_requirements(parent))}
    assert {"pytest", "pluggy", "celery", "redis"} <= names


def test_backend_closure_refuses_a_missing_distribution(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    req = tmp_path / "r.txt"
    req.write_text("dataq-no-such-package-xyz\n", encoding="utf-8")
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="not installed"):
        cl.backend_closure(cl.read_requirements(req))


def test_notices_carry_texts_and_overrides() -> None:
    pkg = cl.Package(
        name="demo",
        version="1.2",
        licence="MIT",
        homepage="https://example.test/demo",
        texts=[("LICENSE", "Copyright (c) Demo\nPermission is hereby granted"), ("NOTICE", "Demo NOTICE")],
        override="declared 'UNKNOWN'; reviewed — https://example.test/LICENSE",
    )
    bare = cl.Package(name="bare", version="0.1", licence="BSD-3-Clause")
    text = cl.render_notices("DataQ backend", [pkg, bare])
    assert "| demo | 1.2 | MIT (reviewed override: see below) | https://example.test/demo |" in text
    assert "Permission is hereby granted" in text and "Demo NOTICE" in text
    assert "Licence override: declared 'UNKNOWN'" in text
    assert "No licence text is shipped in the distribution" in text


def test_frontend_packages_parse_pnpm_json(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    payload = {
        "MIT": [{"name": "b", "versions": ["1.0"], "license": "MIT", "homepage": "https://b"}],
        "Unknown": [{"name": "a", "versions": ["2.0", "2.1"], "license": "Unknown"}],
    }

    def fake_run(cmd: list[str], **_: object) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        assert cmd[:4] == ["pnpm", "licenses", "list", "--json"]
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 0, json.dumps(payload), "")

    monkeypatch.setattr(cl.subprocess, "run", fake_run)
    packages = cl.frontend_packages(prod=False)
    assert [(p.name, p.version, p.licence) for p in packages] == [
        ("a", "2.0, 2.1", "Unknown"),
        ("b", "1.0", "MIT"),
    ]
    assert cl.check("frontend", packages, {}) == 1


def test_main_fails_on_a_forbidden_requirement(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    req = tmp_path / "r.txt"
    req.write_text("pytest\n", encoding="utf-8")
    original = cl.backend_closure

    def poisoned(requirements: list[object]) -> list[object]:
        return [*original(requirements), _pkg("evil-sspl", "SSPL-1.0")]

    monkeypatch.setattr(cl, "backend_closure", poisoned)
    notices = tmp_path / "out.md"
    assert cl.main(["x", "backend", "--requirements", str(req), "--notices", str(notices)]) == 1
    assert not notices.exists()
    monkeypatch.setattr(cl, "backend_closure", original)
    assert cl.main(["x", "backend", "--requirements", str(req), "--notices", str(notices)]) == 0
    assert notices.read_text(encoding="utf-8").startswith("# Third-party notices — DataQ backend")

# Third-party notices & SBOM

> **Who this is for:** anyone redistributing DataQ's images, and the reviewer who has to
> confirm what a release bundles and under which licences. DataQ itself is MIT; every
> dependency it ships is permissive or weak-copyleft, and the notices and bill of materials
> below are generated from the real dependency set on every build, never hand-maintained.

## What ships, and where

| Artifact | Where to find it | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` | `/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` in the **backend** image | every Python package installed into the image's virtualenv — name, version, licence, homepage, the full licence text and any Apache `NOTICE` file shipped with the package |
| `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` | `/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` in the **frontend** image, also served at `https://<your-dataq>/third-party-notices` | every runtime npm package bundled into the web app (build-only tooling is not distributed and is not listed) |
| `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES-backend.md`, `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES-frontend.md` | assets on each [GitHub release](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/releases) | the same two files, extracted from the images that release published |
| `sbom-dataq-backend.spdx.json`, `sbom-dataq-frontend.spdx.json` | assets on each GitHub release (and a workflow artifact of every image build) | an SPDX 2.3 SBOM produced by [Syft](https://github.com/anchore/syft) over the published image: the Python / npm packages **and** the base image's OS packages, with licence data where the package declares it |

The base images' own packages (Debian for the backend, Alpine for the frontend) are
covered by the SBOM, not by the notices file; their licence texts live under
`/usr/share/doc` and `/usr/share/licenses` in the image as the distributions ship them.

## Verify

```bash
# Read the notices straight out of a published image.
docker run --rm --entrypoint cat ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:latest /THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md | less
docker run --rm --entrypoint cat ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-frontend:latest /THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md | less

# From a running deployment.
curl -fsS https://<your-dataq>/third-party-notices | head

# Re-derive the SBOM yourself and compare package lists with the release asset.
syft ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:v1.3.0 -o spdx-json > local.spdx.json
```

## The licence gate

Continuous integration fails a change whose dependency tree — the backend's full
runtime + test requirements, and the frontend's whole lockfile — adds a package under a
strong-copyleft or source-available licence (GPL, AGPL, SSPL, BUSL, Elastic, Commons Clause),
or whose licence cannot be determined from its metadata. Permissive licences (MIT, BSD,
Apache-2.0, ISC, PSF, Unlicense, 0BSD, Zlib, CC0, BlueOak, OFL for bundled fonts) and weak
copyleft with notice preservation (MPL-2.0, LGPL) are allowed; a dual-licensed package passes
when one of its options is allowed. The backend image build runs the same check over the
exact set it installs, so a violation cannot reach a published image either way.

A package whose packaging metadata omits or misstates a licence that is known and
permissive is admitted only through a reviewed override in the repository
(`scripts/licenses/overrides.toml`), which records the SPDX licence, a link to the
upstream licence file as evidence, and the reason. The override cannot admit a forbidden
licence; that would need an architecture-decision-level exception.

The base images' own packages (Debian for the backend, Alpine for the frontend) are
covered by the SBOM, not by the notices file; their licence texts live under
`/usr/share/doc` and `/usr/share/licenses` in the image as the distributions ship them.

## Verify

```bash
# Read the notices straight out of a published image.
docker run --rm --entrypoint cat ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:latest /THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md | less
docker run --rm --entrypoint cat ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-frontend:latest /THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md | less

# From a running deployment.
curl -fsS https://<your-dataq>/third-party-notices | head

# Re-derive the SBOM yourself and compare package lists with the release asset.
syft ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:v1.3.0 -o spdx-json > local.spdx.json
```

## The licence gate

Continuous integration fails a change whose dependency tree — the backend's full
runtime + test requirements, and the frontend's whole lockfile — adds a package under a
strong-copyleft or source-available licence (GPL, AGPL, SSPL, BUSL, Elastic, Commons Clause),
or whose licence cannot be determined from its metadata. Permissive licences (MIT, BSD,
Apache-2.0, ISC, PSF, Unlicense, 0BSD, Zlib, CC0, BlueOak, OFL for bundled fonts) and weak
copyleft with notice preservation (MPL-2.0, LGPL) are allowed; a dual-licensed package passes
when one of its options is allowed. The backend image build runs the same check over the
exact set it installs, so a violation cannot reach a published image either way.

A package whose packaging metadata omits or misstates a licence that is known and
permissive is admitted only through a reviewed override in the repository
(`scripts/licenses/overrides.toml`), which records the SPDX licence, a link to the
upstream licence file as evidence, and the reason. The override cannot admit a forbidden
licence; that would need an architecture-decision-level exception.

## Summary

- **Notices + SBOM in every image and release (ADR 0031 §3).** Both images now carry `/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` — name, version, licence, homepage, the full licence text and any Apache `NOTICE` file for every package actually installed — generated *inside the image build* from the exact dependency set, so it cannot go stale and works for every builder (publish-images, both deploy workflows, local compose). The frontend also serves it at `/third-party-notices`. On a release tag `publish-images.yml` extracts the file from the pushed image (by digest), runs syft for an SPDX 2.3 SBOM per image (OS packages included), and attaches both to the GitHub Release with the same draft-release pattern `publish-client.yml` uses.
- **Licence gate (rule 40).** `scripts/check-licenses.py` walks the installed closure of `backend/requirements-dev.txt` (extras and markers honoured — `celery[redis]`, `uvicorn[standard]` etc. are followed) and the whole frontend lockfile via `pnpm licenses list --json`, evaluates each licence *expression* (AND / OR / WITH / parenthesised; classifier lists `;` = OR, i.e. dual-licensed) against the allowlist, and fails on anything forbidden, unrecognised or `UNKNOWN`. It runs in CI (`backend-test` + `frontend-lint`), in pre-commit on dependency/policy changes (0.8 s), and the backend image build runs the same check over the venv it just built, so a violation cannot reach a published image either.
- **Reviewed overrides.** `scripts/licenses/overrides.toml` admits a package whose metadata omits/misstates a known-permissive licence; every entry needs `license` + `evidence` URL + `reason`, it is side-scoped, optionally version-pinned, **cannot admit a forbidden licence** (the allowlist is re-applied to the override), and is **inert once upstream fixes its metadata** (the linux image resolved `caio 0.12.9`, which already declares Apache-2.0 — the first local image build showed the override silently overwriting a correct declaration, which is why that rule exists).

### Tool choices (all permissive, nothing new shipped in an image)

| Need | Choice | Licence | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Backend inventory + licence texts | stdlib `importlib.metadata` (+ `packaging`, already a transitive of pytest/GX) | — | zero new pins; reads PEP 639 `License-File`/`licenses/` entries and classic `LICENSE*`/`COPYING*`/`NOTICE*` in the dist-info. `pip-licenses` (MIT) was evaluated and dropped: it only adds a dependency to the builder stage for what twenty lines of stdlib do, and its `--allow-only` has no SPDX-expression or override support. |
| Frontend inventory | `pnpm licenses list --json [--prod]` (built into pnpm 9) | MIT | no new dev dependency; `paths` give the package dir to read licence files from |
| Frontend notices renderer | `frontend/scripts/third-party-notices.mjs` (Node, 60 lines) | — | the frontend image's build context is `frontend/` and node:alpine has no Python; the renderer refuses an undeclared licence so it can never quietly ship one |
| SPDX SBOM | `anchore/sbom-action@v0.24.3` (syft) | Apache-2.0 | the only candidate that also covers the base images' apk/deb packages; pinned to the exact release tag |

### Allowlist / overrides / current state

- Allowed: MIT, MIT-0, X11, BSD-*, 0BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, PSF-2.0/Python-2.0, MPL-2.0, LGPL-*, Unlicense, Zlib, CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0 (caniuse-lite data), BlueOak-1.0.0, OFL-1.1 (the bundled `@fontsource` fonts — ADR 0031 already accepted them), HPND. Forbidden/failing: GPL, AGPL, SSPL, BUSL, Elastic, Commons-Clause, Artistic, non-commercial, proprietary, `UNKNOWN`, and anything not recognised.
- **Override list: one entry — `caio`** (fastmcp → py-key-value-aio → aiofile → caio): no licence metadata at all in the 0.9.x wheels, ships `COPYING` = Apache-2.0 text.
- **No current dependency fails the gate.** Backend dev closure 215 packages / runtime closure 185 (mac) and 188 (linux image) / frontend 498 (whole tree) and 148 (shipped) — all clean. `text-unidecode` (Artistic OR GPL) and `openlineage_sql` (UNKNOWN) are present in the local conda env but **not** in any requirements closure (they come from unrelated extras), which is why the gate walks the closure rather than the whole environment.
- Notices: backend 188 packages / 1.1 MB, frontend 148 / 240 KB. Three backend packages ship no licence text in the wheel (`fastmcp-slim`, `opentelemetry-util-http`, `thrift`) and are listed with a pointer to their homepage.

### Ruleset question

No new required check: both gate steps are folded into existing required jobs (`Backend — tests`, which is the one job with `requirements-dev.txt` installed, and `Frontend — lint & format`). The main ruleset needs no edit. `publish-images.yml`'s job gets `contents: write` (job-level, same as `publish-client.yml`) so it can upload release assets.

## Linked issue

Closes #2387

- [x] **Conventional commit title** (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`)
- [x] **No secrets, credentials, or `.env` files committed**

- [x] **Tests added/updated** (the ≥80% coverage gate is CI-enforced)

- [x] **Docs / ADRs updated** if user-facing or architectural change
